_comment: 3D geometry of the active LED marker array, plus the camera intrinsics needed to turn 2D LED detections into a 6-DoF pose. Used by track_markers_3d.py. Frequencies here must match active_markers.json (the frequency table shared with the Arduino firmware); this file adds WHERE each LED sits on the rig. Pose accuracy is limited directly by how well these numbers match the physical array.

camera._comment: 5 mm CCTV lens on the EVK4 (IMX636, 1280x720, 4.86 um pitch). f = 5.0/0.00486 = 1028.8 px, giving 63.8 x 38.6 deg (71.0 deg diagonal). The 1/1.7in image circle covers the 7.14 mm sensor diagonal with room to spare. WARNING: this derived matrix assumes a perfect pinhole with the principal point at the image centre and ZERO distortion. A 5 mm CCTV lens has real barrel distortion - several pixels near the frame edge - and every one of those pixels turns straight into pose error. Run metavision_mono_calibration and paste camera_matrix and dist_coeffs here before trusting any number this pipeline prints.

array._comment: Coordinates below are in the ARRAY frame: origin at the PCB centre, +X towards the USB connector end, +Y down, +Z away from the camera. The two on-board LED positions come from Arduino's own Eagle board file (ABX00030-cad-files.zip, NANO33BLE_V4.0.brd), converted from its bottom-left origin to this centred frame; the board outline there is 43.18 x 17.78 mm.

_on_board_led_survey._comment: Every LED on the Nano 33 BLE, from the manufacturer's board file, so it is clear what is and is not available as a marker.
leds: DL1 YELLOW  @ (1.90, 3.10)   -> R3 -> net SCK = D13. The user LED. USABLE as a marker.
DL2 GREEN   @ (1.90, 14.70)  -> R2 -> power rail. Always on, never blinks, so it emits no events and CANNOT be a marker.
DL3 RGB     @ (26.65, 12.50) -> R7/R11/R12 -> LEDR/LEDG/LEDB. One package, three dies, ONE position. Usable, but contributes only ONE marker point no matter how many channels are driven.
_on_board_led_survey.conclusion: The PCB can supply at most TWO distinct marker positions, 26.47 mm apart. Two points cannot determine a 6-DoF pose. At least two more physically separated LEDs must be added on free pins before this pipeline can solve anything.

_how_to_measure_added_leds: 1. Keep the origin at the PCB centre and the axes above, so the two on-board LEDs stay valid.
2. Measure each added LED's emitting centre relative to that origin, not its pad or package edge.
3. Leave Z at 0.0 for anything mounted flat on the board plane.
4. Raising ONE LED out of the plane by 15-25 mm removes the planar mirror ambiguity entirely; it is the cheapest accuracy win available.
5. Set measured=true per LED once its numbers are real.

_sizing._comment: Median pose error from a 200-trial synthetic sweep with this lens, 0.5 px centroid noise, 4 LEDs at the corners of a square array (see the sizing study). Accuracy scales with the array's apparent size in pixels, so the array span and the working range trade off directly.

_geometry_requirements: 6-DoF pose needs at least 4 LEDs that are not collinear; 4 is the practical minimum and more is better.
3 LEDs is solvable (P3P) but returns up to 4 candidate poses with no way to choose between them from one frame.
2 LEDs cannot give a 6-DoF pose at all: rotation about the line joining them is unobservable.
Spread the LEDs as widely as the rig allows - a board-sized 43 mm array is only usable to about half a metre with this lens.
